short: Generalized star height at most three

title.title: Generalized star height at most three
title.subtitle: Claim: every regular language has a generalized regular expression with at most three nested stars

plain: Search patterns with 'not' allowed never need more than three nested repeat-loops, for any regular pattern

object.axisLabel: a uniform bound on generalized star height

beats.text: With complement allowed, no uniform bound on nested stars was known at all
This family brings it to 13, then 4, then 3
Whether one star always suffices is still the open problem

steps: Treat the pattern as a small machine reading a word
Cut every word into uniquely marked pieces
Pass the machine state across each cut with simple tests
Two nested cuts on simple tests reach height three

achievement.note: Expression size is unbounded; whether height 1 suffices is still open

verify.detail: GeneralizedStarHeight.lean for the bound 3, which subsumes 13 and 4
verify.ourCheck: We did not build the Lean or referee the proof

voice.text: With complement allowed, nobody could prove any fixed bound on nested stars.
Cut every word into marked pieces, twice, passing the state across each cut.
Claimed: three nested stars always suffice.

sources.quote: Earlier papers in the family give bounds 13 and 4.
No uniform bound of any size was known.
Does not decide whether height 1 suffices
GeneralizedStarHeight.lean (OAI.GeneralizedStarHeight.main) for the bound 3, which subsumes the 13 and 4 papers
